apps.localizedDescription:
🔥 FlameLauncher for iOS:

Run Minecraft: Java Edition on iPhone and iPad.

• What it does:.

This is Java Edition, not Bedrock. Join the servers your PC friends use, run the mods they run. A real OpenJDK boots inside the app process — this is not an emulator.

Graphics:

The renderer is per-instance. Shaders require MobileGlues.

Controls:

• On-screen buttons — you place and size them yourself.
• Hardware keyboard — picked up as soon as it connects.
• Gamepad — sticks and triggers included.
• In-game menu — change resolution and hotbar size while playing.

Multiplayer:

Ordinary servers, plus Online LAN for playing with a friend without renting a server: open a room, share the code, they join with it.

versions.localizedDescription:
What's new:

• FlameJIT, a small companion app that turns JIT on for you. Install it next to FlameLauncher and the launcher hands it the process, the pairing file and the JIT script over a URL; it attaches and returns. No picking the app in StikDebug, no re-selecting a script after every reinstall. It keeps no state of its own. It has to be a separate app: a process that attaches a debugger to itself deadlocks, and the in-app helper extension route (AppExtensionProcess) is iOS 26 only, which would have left iPads out. A loopback tunnel is still required — install LocalDevVPN and connect it once.
• The pairing file is kept in the keychain. Drop it in once (from a Mac, the Files app, or the new picker in Settings) and reinstalling the launcher no longer loses it. The file is recognised by its contents, so a lockdown pair record — which the tunnel rejects — is no longer mistaken for one.
• Minecraft now runs on iPads that have TXM but are not on iOS 26 (the M2 iPad on iPadOS 18.6, for one). The mirrored code cache was gated on the OS version, but TXM arrived earlier; on those devices MAP_JIT is refused even with a debugger attached, and the JVM died right after Using G1.
• The launcher no longer crashes when the JIT helper returns. Declaring a URL scheme without implementing application(_:open:options:) makes UIKit abort the app — which it did, one second after JIT was successfully enabled.
• Heavy modpacks survive startup. The off-heap estimate was measured on the Vulkan path; on the OpenGL path ANGLE holds its textures in app memory and the real figure is about 1.4 GB, so the heap ceiling was too generous and iOS killed the app seconds after the game finished loading. A heap size saved on a roomier day is now trimmed to what the device can take at launch.
